previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic breast cancer and a history of gastroparesis was readmitted three days after discharge due to recurrent nausea and vomiting. She had completed a course of vancomycin for C. difficile colitis and was found to be malnourished. A GJ tube was placed on hospital day two, and jejunal feeding was initiated to address nutritional needs and prevent refeeding syndrome. She tolerated tube feeds well, with gradual improvement in symptoms. Her medications were continued, except for holding Denosumab pending oncology follow-up. She was discharged home with services, on a regimen of continuous tube feeds, oral supplements, and home medications, with plans for outpatient follow-up in gastroenterology and oncology.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with mets breast cancer, refractory idiopathic
gastroparesis w/G-J tube. Multiple admissions for N/V, presents ___ for
clogged G-J tube. ___ ___ placed 16 ___ MIC G-J tube.// G-J tube check

COMPARISON:  GJ placement ___

TECHNIQUE:   OPERATORS: Dr. ___ Interventional ___ and
Dr. ___, Interventional Radiology fellow performed the procedure.
Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during any key components of
the procedure where applicable and reviewed and agrees with the findings as
reported below.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
100mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 35 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: None
CONTRAST: 20 ml of Optiray contrast
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 4.1 minutes, 16 mGy


PROCEDURE:  1.  Exchange of a gastrojejunostomy tube.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The upper abdomen and tube site was prepped and draped in the usual
sterile fashion.
The existing tube was clogged and broken near the skin entry site and could
not be injected with contrast.  The stay sutures were cut. A stiff glide wire
was advanced through the tube into the stomach. The existing tube was then
removed using gentle traction. A 16 ___ mic gastrojejunostomy tube was
advanced over the wire into the stomach and the balloon was inflated using
contrast diluted in sterile water. Contrast injection confirmed appropriate
position of the gastric and jejunal lumens.  The tube was secured in place
using 0 silk sutures. Sterile dressing was applied. Patient tolerated the
procedure well and there were no immediate post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS: 

1. 16 ___ mic gastrojejunostomy tube in the jejunum.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful exchange of a gastrojejunostomy tube for a new 16 ___ mic
gastrojejunostomy tube. The tube is ready to use.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ Interventional ___ and

ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
75mcg of fentanyl and 1.5 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 30 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: 1% lidocaine
CONTRAST: 30 cc ml of Optiray contrast
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 2 minutes 47 seconds, 13 mGy

PROCEDURE:  MIC gastrojejunostomy exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The tube site was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

The existing tube could not be injected because it was completely clogged. The
stay sutures were cut and a 0.035 stiff Glidewire was advanced into the
stomach.  The existing feeding tube was then removed.  A 18 ___ Fr MIC
gastrojejunostomy catheter was advanced over the wire into position.  The
balloon was inflated and pulled back against the anterior wall of the stomach.
Position was confirmed with contrast injection through the jejunostomy and
gastrostomy lumens.

The catheter was then flushed, capped and secured. Sterile dressings were
applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.

FINDINGS: 

1.  Clogged 16 ___ gastrojejunostomy catheter.
2.  Appropriately positioned new 18 ___ MIC gastrojejunostomy tube.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful exchange of a ___ clogged gastrojejunostomy tube for a new 18
___ MIC gastrojejunostomy tube. The tube is ready to use.
